name: ABS
about: Gives a number without its minus sign.

example.why: The minus sign is dropped, so -450 becomes 450.

name: ACOS

args.name: number
args.about: the cosine of the angle, from -1 to 1

about: Gives the angle, in radians, whose cosine is the number.

example.why: The angle with a cosine of 0.5 is 60 degrees, which is π/3 radians.

notes: Wrap it in DEGREES to get the angle in degrees.

name: ACOSH
about: Gives the inverse hyperbolic cosine of a number.

example.why: COSH(0) is 1, so ACOSH(1) is 0.

name: ASIN

args.name: number
args.about: the sine of the angle, from -1 to 1

about: Gives the angle, in radians, whose sine is the number.

example.why: The angle with a sine of 1 is 90 degrees, which is π/2 radians.

notes: Wrap it in DEGREES to get the angle in degrees.

name: ASINH
about: Gives the inverse hyperbolic sine of a number.

example.why: SINH(0) is 0, so ASINH(0) is 0.

name: ATAN
about: Gives the angle, in radians, whose tangent is the number.

example.why: The angle with a tangent of 1 is 45 degrees, which is π/4 radians.

notes: ATAN2 takes x and y separately and knows which quarter the angle is in.

name: ATAN2

args.name: x_num
args.about: how far across the point is

args.name: y_num
args.about: how far up the point is

about: Gives the angle, in radians, from the x axis to a point.

example.why: The point (-1, 1) is up and to the left, at 135 degrees, which is 3π/4 radians.

notes: x comes first, as in other spreadsheet apps (many programming languages put y first).

name: ATANH
about: Gives the inverse hyperbolic tangent of a number.

name: COS
about: Gives the cosine of an angle.

example.why: 60 degrees turned into radians has a cosine of 0.5.

name: COSH
about: Gives the hyperbolic cosine of a number.

name: LOG

args.name: base
args.about: the base of the logarithm (10 if left out)

about: Gives the power the base must be raised to to make the number.

example.why: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, so the logarithm of 8 in base 2 is 3.

name: LOG10
about: Gives the base-10 logarithm of a number.

example.why: 10 to the power 3 is 1000.

name: LN
about: Gives the natural logarithm of a number (base e).

example.why: e to the power 0 is 1.

notes: EXP does the opposite.

name: MAX

args.name: number1
args.about: a number, a cell or a range

about: Gives the largest number.

example.why: 150 is the biggest of 120, 80 and 150.

name: MIN

args.name: number1
args.about: a number, a cell or a range

about: Gives the smallest number.

example.why: 80 is the smallest of 120, 80 and 150.

name: PI
about: Gives π, the distance round a circle divided by its width.

example.why: π, shown to ten figures; the cell holds it to about 15.

name: POWER

args.name: power
args.about: how many times to multiply it by itself

about: Raises a number to a power.
notes: The ^ sign does the same: =A2^B2.

name: PRODUCT

args.name: number1
args.about: a number, a cell or a range to multiply

about: Multiplies numbers together.

name: RAND
about: Gives a random number from 0 up to (but not including) 1.

example.why: A new number is picked each time the sheet works itself out again.

notes: RANDBETWEEN gives whole numbers in a range.

name: RANDBETWEEN

args.name: bottom
args.about: the smallest number it may give

args.name: top
args.about: the largest number it may give

about: Gives a random whole number between two numbers.

example.why: Like a die: any whole number from 1 to 6, new each time the sheet works itself out.

name: ROUND

args.name: num_digits
args.about: how many decimal places to keep (negative rounds to tens, hundreds…)

about: Rounds a number to a number of decimal places.

example.why: The third decimal is 6, so the second rounds up from 4 to 5.

notes: ROUNDUP and ROUNDDOWN always round one way.

name: ROUNDDOWN

args.name: num_digits
args.about: how many decimal places to keep

about: Rounds a number towards zero.

example.why: Everything after the second decimal is cut off.

name: ROUNDUP

args.name: num_digits
args.about: how many decimal places to keep

about: Rounds a number away from zero.

example.why: Anything after the second decimal pushes it up to the next hundredth.

name: SIN
about: Gives the sine of an angle.

example.why: 30 degrees turned into radians has a sine of 0.5.

name: SINH
about: Gives the hyperbolic sine of a number.

name: SQRT
about: Gives the square root of a number.

example.why: 12 × 12 = 144, so a square of 144 m² has 12 m sides.

name: SQRTPI

args.name: number
args.about: a number of 0 or more to multiply by π

about: Gives the square root of a number times π.

example.why: The square root of 1 × π is 1.7724…

name: SUM

args.name: number1
args.about: a number, a cell or a range of cells to add up

about: Adds up numbers.

example.why: 120 + 80 + 150 = 350. Words in the range are left out.

name: SUMIF

args.name: sum_range
args.about: the cells to add up (the tested cells if left out)

about: Adds up the numbers in rows that pass a test.

example.why: Only the Apple rows count: 3 + 4.

notes: SUMIFS takes more than one test.

name: SUMIFS

args.name: criteria_range1
args.about: the cells for the first test

args.name: criteria_range2
args.about: the cells for the next test

about: Adds up the numbers in rows that pass every test.

example.why: Only apples sold in the North shop count: 3 + 2.

notes: Unlike SUMIF, the cells to add up come first.

name: SUMX2MY2

args.name: array_y
args.about: the second list, the same size

about: Adds up the differences of the squares of matching numbers in two lists.

name: SUMX2PY2

args.name: array_y
args.about: the second list, the same size

about: Adds up the squares of all the numbers in two lists.

name: SUMXMY2

args.name: array_y
args.about: the second list, the same size

about: Adds up the squares of the differences between matching numbers in two lists.

name: TAN
about: Gives the tangent of an angle.

example.why: At 45 degrees the opposite and adjacent sides are the same length.

name: TANH
about: Gives the hyperbolic tangent of a number.

name: ACOT
about: Gives the angle, in radians, whose cotangent is the number.

example.why: The angle with a cotangent of 1 is 45 degrees, which is π/4 radians.

name: ACOTH
about: Gives the inverse hyperbolic cotangent of a number.

example.why: It is ATANH of 1/2.

name: COT
about: Gives the cotangent of an angle (1 divided by its tangent).

example.why: The tangent of 45 degrees is 1, and 1/1 is 1.

name: COTH
about: Gives the hyperbolic cotangent of a number.

name: CSC
about: Gives the cosecant of an angle (1 divided by its sine).

example.why: The sine of 30 degrees is 0.5, and 1/0.5 is 2.

name: CSCH
about: Gives the hyperbolic cosecant of a number.

name: SEC
about: Gives the secant of an angle (1 divided by its cosine).

example.why: The cosine of 60 degrees is 0.5, and 1/0.5 is 2.

name: SECH
about: Gives the hyperbolic secant of a number.

name: EXP

args.name: number
args.about: the power to raise e to

about: Gives e (2.71828…) raised to a power.

example.why: e to the power 1 is e itself.

notes: LN does the opposite.

name: FACT

args.name: number
args.about: a whole number of 0 or more

about: Gives the factorial of a number: 1 × 2 × 3 … up to it.

example.why: Five guests can sit in a row in 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 × 5 = 120 ways.

name: FACTDOUBLE

args.name: number
args.about: a whole number of 0 or more

about: Gives the double factorial: the number times every second number below it.

name: SIGN
about: Gives 1 for a positive number, -1 for a negative one and 0 for zero.

example.why: -450 is below zero.

name: RADIANS
about: Turns degrees into radians.

example.why: Half a turn, 180 degrees, is π radians.

name: DEGREES
about: Turns radians into degrees.

example.why: π/2 radians is a quarter turn, 90 degrees.

name: INT
about: Rounds a number down to the whole number below it.

example.why: It always rounds down, so -3.7 goes to -4.

notes: TRUNC just cuts off the decimals, giving -3 here.

name: EVEN
about: Rounds a number away from zero to the next even whole number.

example.why: Seats come in pairs, so 7 guests need 8 seats.

name: ODD
about: Rounds a number away from zero to the next odd whole number.

example.why: 3 is the first odd whole number above 2.1.

name: CEILING

args.name: significance
args.about: the multiple to round up to

about: Rounds a number up to the next multiple of another.

example.why: 4.45 is the next multiple of 0.05 at or above 4.42.

notes: An older function: CEILING.MATH works the same for positive numbers and is clearer with negative ones.

name: CEILING.MATH

args.name: significance
args.about: the multiple to round to (1 if left out)

args.name: mode
args.about: for negative numbers: 0 or left out rounds towards zero, anything else away from it

about: Rounds a number up to the next multiple.

example.why: With tables of six, 23 people need room for 24.

name: CEILING.PRECISE

args.name: significance
args.about: the multiple to round to (1 if left out)

about: Rounds a number up to the next multiple, whatever the signs.

example.why: Up means towards plus, so -4.3 goes to -4.

name: FLOOR

args.name: significance
args.about: the multiple to round down to

about: Rounds a number down to a multiple of another.

example.why: 4.45 is the multiple of 0.05 at or just below 4.48.

notes: An older function: FLOOR.MATH works the same for positive numbers and is clearer with negative ones.

name: FLOOR.MATH

args.name: significance
args.about: the multiple to round to (1 if left out)

args.name: mode
args.about: for negative numbers: 0 or left out rounds away from zero, anything else towards it

about: Rounds a number down to a multiple.

example.why: 29 eggs fill four boxes of six, which hold 24.

name: FLOOR.PRECISE

args.name: significance
args.about: the multiple to round to (1 if left out)

about: Rounds a number down to a multiple, whatever the signs.

example.why: Down means towards minus, so -4.3 goes to -6.

name: ISO.CEILING

args.name: significance
args.about: the multiple to round to (1 if left out)

about: Rounds a number up to the next multiple, whatever the signs.

example.why: 6 is the next multiple of 2 above 4.3.

notes: The same as CEILING.PRECISE.

name: MOD
about: Gives what is left over after dividing.

example.why: Each child gets 3 sweets (15 in all) and 2 are left over.

notes: QUOTIENT gives the whole part of the division.

name: QUOTIENT
about: Divides and gives only the whole part of the answer.

example.why: 17 / 5 is 3.4, so each child gets 3 whole sweets.

notes: MOD gives what is left over.

name: MROUND
about: Rounds a number to the nearest multiple.

example.why: 37 is nearer 30 than 45.

name: TRUNC

args.name: num_digits
args.about: how many decimal places to keep (0 if left out)

about: Cuts off a number's decimals without rounding.

example.why: The .7 is just dropped.

notes: INT rounds down instead, giving -4 here.

name: GCD

args.name: number1
args.about: a whole number or a range

about: Gives the largest whole number that divides all the numbers exactly.

example.why: 12 goes into both 24 and 36, and nothing bigger does.

name: LCM

args.name: number1
args.about: a whole number or a range

about: Gives the smallest number that all the numbers divide into exactly.

example.why: Buses every 4 and every 6 minutes leave together again after 12 minutes.

name: BASE

args.name: number
args.about: a whole number of 0 or more

args.name: radix
args.about: the base to write it in, from 2 to 36

args.name: min_length
args.about: pad with zeros to at least this many characters

about: Writes a number in another base, as text.

example.why: 10 in binary is 1010, padded to eight characters.

notes: DECIMAL does the opposite.

name: DECIMAL

args.name: text
args.about: a number written in another base

args.name: radix
args.about: the base it is written in, from 2 to 36

about: Turns a number written in another base into an ordinary number.

example.why: FF in base 16 is 15 × 16 + 15 = 255.

notes: BASE does the opposite.

name: ROMAN

args.name: form
args.about: 0 or left out for the classic form; 1 to 4 for shorter ones

about: Writes a number in Roman numerals.
notes: ARABIC does the opposite.

name: ARABIC
about: Turns Roman numerals into an ordinary number.
notes: ROMAN does the opposite.

name: COMBIN
about: Gives how many ways there are to pick some things from a group, when order doesn't matter.

example.why: From 5 players you can make 10 different pairs.

notes: COMBINA lets the same thing be picked more than once.

name: COMBINA
about: Gives how many ways there are to pick some things from a group, when each may be picked again.

example.why: Two scoops from 3 flavours, doubles allowed, make 6 different cones.

name: SUMSQ

args.name: number1
args.about: a number, a cell or a range

about: Adds up the squares of numbers.

name: MDETERM
about: Gives the determinant of a square block of numbers.

name: MINVERSE
about: Gives the inverse of a square block of numbers.

example.why: The inverse is 0.6, -0.7, -0.2, 0.4, spilling into a 2 × 2 block; 0.6 is its first cell.

name: MUNIT
about: Gives a square block with 1 down the diagonal and 0 everywhere else.

example.why: It spills a 3 × 3 block; the first cell is on the diagonal, so it is 1.

name: MULTINOMIAL

args.name: number1
args.about: a whole number of 0 or more

about: Gives how many ways there are to split things into groups of given sizes.

name: SERIESSUM

args.name: x
args.about: the value to put into the series

args.name: n
args.about: the power of x for the first term

args.name: m
args.about: how much the power goes up each term

args.name: coefficients
args.about: the numbers to multiply each term by

about: Adds up a power series: a₁xⁿ + a₂xⁿ⁺ᵐ + a₃xⁿ⁺²ᵐ…

name: SUMPRODUCT

args.name: array2
args.about: more ranges the same size to multiply with it

about: Multiplies matching numbers in ranges and adds up the results.

name: PERCENTOF

args.name: data_subset
args.about: the part, as numbers or a range

args.name: data_all
args.about: the whole, as numbers or a range

about: Gives what share of a total a part makes up.

example.why: 120 out of a total of 400 is 0.3, or 30%.

name: SUBTOTAL

args.name: function_num
args.about: which sum to do: 9 adds up, 1 averages, 2 counts…; add 100 to skip hidden rows

about: Works out a sum, average, count or the like over a range, leaving out other subtotals.

example.why: Function 1 is the average: 350 / 3.

notes: Codes: 1 AVERAGE, 2 COUNT, 3 COUNTA, 4 MAX, 5 MIN, 6 PRODUCT, 7 STDEV, 8 STDEVP, 9 SUM, 10 VAR, 11 VARP.
